newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar succumbs to selling at close.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar succumbs to selling at close.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed just off its lows on Monday and dealers expect further selling pressure leading up to the Reserve Bank Monetary Policy Statement on Friday.
It closed at 5.15 p.m. (0515 GMT) at US$0.6827/34 against its 0.6843/50 opening, having traded a 0.6825-48 range.

Despite the U.S. market being closed, a couple of U.S. names sold the Kiwi through the day. However, buyers absorbed the selling and the currency is only seen dropping sharply if key support at 0.6810 is smashed.
A weakening trend is predicted for the week as expectations for the size of the Reserve Bank's easing on Friday are raised.
Most players now expect the RB to sanction a 75 point easing, against earlier expectations of 50 basis points.
But some said the new expectations are overly optimistic.
"I think its unrealistic. People are saying at least three quarters. I think maximum three quarters and probably a half," said one dealer.
Thursday's budget is seen having little effect on the currency.
The Trade-Weighted Index closed at 67.18 from its 67.26 opening.
